claims.text: TOR-TILD conventionally uses empirical EAM reference potentials.
EAM reference potentials poorly represent the configurational diversity of ab initio high-temperature liquids.
The proposed intervention is to replace the EAM reference with a DNN potential trained on ab initio liquid and solid configurations.
A trained machine-learning potential can accurately predict energies for solid and disordered high-temperature configurations.
The proposed DNN incorporates many-body interactions.
Training on a comprehensive set of ab initio liquid configurations will allow the DNN to emulate the complex target energy landscape better than EAM.
The DNN will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The DNN reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The DNN reference will yield latent heats of fusion or melting temperatures closer to direct ab initio results.
The method applies near melting over approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
The intended materials include equimolar multicomponent systems such as Ti-Zr-Ta-Hf-Nb-based carbides or nitrides in both solid and liquid states.
The method is expected to be most effective for high-melting alloys with substantial configurational diversity.
Benefits may be limited for less configurationally complex alloys or temperatures far from melting.
The exact mismatch reduction and optimal composition and temperature training ranges remain undetermined.
Generalization to high-entropy alloys beyond the studied systems has not been fully validated.
Failure to obtain at least an approximately 50% mismatch reduction or any phase-space-overlap improvement would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of DNN-derived free energies to converge significantly toward direct ab initio values would falsify the hypothesis.
